tier_rationale: The manufacturer's own datasheet gives a full port diagram and connectivity table: HDMI 1.4, DisplayPort 1.2, VGA, USB 3.2 Type-B upstream, three USB 3.2 Type-A downstream, and one USB-C downstream (data/power only). No Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet, camera, or microphone appears anywhere in the specification. It is a passive display panel that only shows whatever is fed to it over a video cable. The datasheet's 'Remote Asset Management: Yes' line is now resolved and does not disturb the D0: Dell's own DDPM documentation states 'DDPM requires DDC/CI (Display Data Channel/Command Interface) to communicate with your monitor' — DDC/CI is a sideband channel on the video cable itself, not a network. Where a cloud appears in this feature it is the host PC talking to Dell's management console; the firewall rules Dell publishes for it are rules for the PC. The monitor has no network path of its own to permit or block. 'Remote' here describes an IT admin managing the computer, not the display reaching anyone.
the_unplug_test: It just shows whatever is plugged into it. This monitor has no operating system, no smart platform, no camera, and no network interface of its own — the on-screen menu is navigated with a physical joystick and every setting lives in the monitor's own memory. 'Dell Display and Peripheral Manager' software and 'remote asset management' mentioned in Dell's materials run on the connected PC and reach the monitor over the same USB or video cable already plugged in, not over a network connection the monitor itself makes.

repairability.notes: VESA 100x100mm mount, replaceable stand, standard external power brick; Dell's 3-year Advanced Exchange and Premium Panel Exchange programs cover the panel during warranty.

sources.supports: Manufacturer datasheet 'Ports & Slots' diagram and 'Technical Specification' table: connectivity limited to HDMI 1.4, DisplayPort 1.2, VGA, USB 3.2 Gen1 Type-B upstream, 3x USB 3.2 Type-A downstream, and USB-C downstream (data only, 15W PD) — no Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Ethernet, camera, or microphone listed anywhere in the 10-page document. Audio output is via an optional sold-separately soundbar accessory, not a built-in speaker or radio.

Dell's own DDPM support article: 'DDPM requires DDC/CI (Display Data Channel/Command Interface) to communicate with your monitor', and 'Without DDC/CI enabled, only the Easy Arrange feature works'. Establishes that the datasheet's 'Remote Asset Management' feature reaches the monitor over the video cable's DDC/CI sideband, not over any network. The article's network requirements — outgoing/incoming ports 5566-5568 to Dell servers — are firewall rules for the HOST PC running DDPM, confirming the internet leg belongs to the computer rather than the display.

open_questions: No FCC-grantee search was run given the manufacturer's own complete port list shows no radio; a search would only add value if that list were in doubt.
notes: The predecessor model (P2422H) appears to be discontinued from Dell's own store as of September 2026 with the P2425H as its direct successor in the Pro/P-series line; buyers should check Dell's current P-series naming, which has churned (P2422H to P2425H to 'Dell Pro 24 Plus Monitor') without changing the fundamental fact that these office monitors carry no network stack.

changelog.change: Resolved the record's one hedge on its own deciding fact. The datasheet's unexplained 'Remote Asset Management: Yes' is DDC/CI over the video cable per Dell's own DDPM documentation; the cloud leg belongs to the host PC. D0 unchanged and now unhedged.
